subject: Renewal negotiation: capacity commitments, benchmark findings, and commercial proposal
messages:
From: Emily Chen <procurement@peakcommerce.com>
To: Lukas Meyer <lukas@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-01T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Contract renewal - capacity review & RFP benchmarking

Hi Lukas,

We're kicking off the renewal conversation for our inference platform and I wanted to share high-level findings from the benchmarking run we completed with our infra team. We've had internal pressure around per-token unit cost and sustained tail latencies at 95th/99th for peak ETL windows. We ran Redwood (current prod bundle) vs two vendors (GaleAI and NimbusML) across our top 10 traffic templates.

Quick summary:
- GaleAI beat us on headline per-token price in the quote they provided (they quoted a 20% lower committed unit)
- Redwood showed better 99th latency stability for long-context workloads, but our SREs are concerned about burst capacity during promotions
- The procurement team needs: a commercial adjustment and an operational guarantee (burst capacity + response SLA) to renew at current seat counts

I've attached the detailed spreadsheet (peak-benchmark-results.xlsx). Would appreciate a commercial response and any ops commitments you can provide by end of next week — we have an internal decision window on 8/20.

Thanks,
Emily Chen
Head of Procurement, PeakCommerce

Attachment: peak-benchmark-results.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

From: Lukas Meyer <lukas@redwood.com>
To: Emily Chen <procurement@peakcommerce.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-03T11:06:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Contract renewal - capacity review & RFP benchmarking

Hi Emily — thanks for the data and the clear ask. I reviewed the spreadsheet and appreciate the detail.

Short version: we can close the commercial gap and address the burst/SLO concerns, but we need to propose a concrete, timebound plan that gives PeakCommerce predictability (cost + committed throughput) and preserves Redwood's ability to optimize operational overhead.

Proposed next steps from us:
1) 2-week pilot (no change to production routing) to validate your peak promotion workload with a dedicated burst pool for those windows
2) A committed-capacity option (reserved GPU pool + predictable unit pricing) with a 12-month term or optional 24-month with additional discount — I'll put two commercial options in writing
3) Service commitments: documented burst guarantee, 99th latency SLO for long-context templates, and a monthly capacity review cadence

Marissa — can you and SRE own the pilot scope with PeakCommerce and confirm what we can promise for burst pool sizing? Dylan, can you provide the rough ops guardrails (warming time, prefetch cache sizing) we should include in the SOW?

Emily — we'll aim to get a formal offer and SOW draft to you by Friday 8/14. If the timeline is tight on your side, let me know and we'll accelerate.

Best,
Lukas Meyer
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Emily Chen <procurement@peakcommerce.com>
To: Lukas Meyer <lukas@redwood.com>
Cc: Victor Ramos <victor.ramos@peakcommerce.com>
Date: 2026-08-05T08:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Contract renewal - capacity review & RFP benchmarking

Lukas — thanks. Attaching a short PDF summary (benchmark-summary.pdf) that our infra lead pulled together highlighting the cost delta and the competitor commercial terms (anonymized). A couple clarifications:
- PeakCommerce is comfortable with a 12-month committed plan if the committed unit price is within 10% of the competitor quote and if there is a burst protection mechanism for at least 2x baseline for 8 hours during promos
- We want a one-way migration/rollback playbook documented in the SOW if performance regressions occur after cutover

We have a VP Eng alignment meeting on 8/18 where the preferred commercial will be presented. Can you confirm by 8/14 with a specific number and the SLO language?

Emily
Attachment: benchmark-summary.pdf (pdf stub)

From: Lukas Meyer <lukas@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-06T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: PeakCommerce benchmark summary — need option set and SLO language

Marissa / Dylan — forwarding Emily's request + summary. Key asks:
- Committed unit within 10% of competitor (they shared a redacted quote)
- Dedicated burst pool that can sustain 2x baseline for an 8-hour window during promotions
- Documented rollback playbook in the SOW

My thinking on options:
A) Protection Plan (12 months) — reserved pool sized to current steady-state + 50% buffer, 10% price concession vs current renewal quote, monthly capacity reviews, and up to 2 promotional bursts (8 hours each) included. Performance credits: pro-rated credits for SLO misses (99th latency).
B) Scale Plan (24 months) — deeper price concession (15%), guaranteed access to larger burst pool with pre-warmed instances for promotions, onboarding discount for first 3 months.

Ops notes from Dylan needed: how quickly can we spin up the pre-warmed burst capacity and what's the realistic upper bound for their promo peak given their traffic shapes? Also, legal prefers a rollback clause with a 3-business-day remediation window before migration is reversed.

This is higher urgency — VP Eng decision 8/18. I can include an exec sponsor call with VP Sales if that helps lock it.

Thanks,
Lukas

Quoted: "Emily — please confirm the timing constraints and any hard procurement limits."

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Lukas Meyer <lukas@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-07T14:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: PeakCommerce benchmark summary — need option set and SLO language

Lukas — I added language and concrete numbers to the two-option approach. Edits below (high level):

Option A — Protection Plan (12mo)
- Reserved pool: steady-state baseline + 50% buffer; included bursts: 2x baseline for up to 8 hours, up to 2 promo events per quarter
- Commercial: 8% effective unit discount vs current renewal quote if they commit today; cap on overage pricing at +25% of committed rate
- SLOs: 99th latency target < 350ms for long-context templates; monthly performance report; credits = 5% of monthly invoice per qualified SLO miss (cumulative cap 30%)
- Rollback: documented playbook, with 3-business-day remediation and final rollback decision window

Option B — Scale Plan (24mo)
- Reserved pool + pre-warmed burst lane (spin-up < 60 minutes for warmed instances)
- Commercial: 14% discount vs current renewal quote and 3-month onboarding credit
- SLOs: tighter latency target (99th < 300ms) and priority triage channel

Also recommend an executive alignment call — propose Wed 8/12 or Thurs 8/13 (VP Sales + Head of Solutions) to walk the options. If PeakCommerce signs up for Option A by 8/14 we can include a one-time professional services credit to cover the pilot and initial tuning.

I'll prepare the revised SOW and pricing spreadsheet for Lukas to send.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Lukas Meyer <lukas@redwood.com>
To: Emily Chen <procurement@peakcommerce.com>, Victor Ramos <victor.ramos@peakcommerce.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-14T16:42:00-07:00
Subject: Proposal: PeakCommerce renewal options (Protection Plan / Scale Plan) + SOW

Hi Emily / Victor — thanks for the patience while we pulled internal ops, legal, and solutions together. Attached are two formal options and the related SOW/pricing: redwood-revised-sow.docx and redwood-pricing-commitment.xlsx. High level:

Option A — Protection Plan (12mo):
- Reserved capacity = baseline + 50% buffer, two promotional burst events included (2x baseline, 8 hours max each)
- Effective unit price = current renewal quote - 8%
- SLOs: 99th latency target < 350ms for key templates; monthly performance reports; credits for missed SLOs
- Rollback playbook and remediation window documented in SOW

Option B — Scale Plan (24mo):
- Deeper discount (14% off current renewal quote), pre-warmed burst lane with <60 minute warm-up, 3 months onboarding credit
- Tighter SLO: 99th < 300ms and priority triage during promos

Commitment & next steps:
- If PeakCommerce confirms Option A by 2026-08-14 we will:
  - Include a one-time professional services credit to fund the pilot and tuning
  - Deliver a DocuSign envelope with the SOW and commercial terms for signature (link below)
- DocuSign (preview): https://www.docusign.com/signed/XYZ-PEAK-2026
\Attachments: redwood-revised-sow.docx (docx stub), redwood-pricing-commitment.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

Please let me know which option you prefer and we can schedule the exec alignment call this week. Happy to jump on Victor's 8/18 VP Eng meeting if helpful.

Best,
Lukas Meyer
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
